source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 6 (Control and Coordination).

sections.heading: 1. Nervous System — Basics
points: **Control and coordination** in animals is done by the **nervous system** and the **endocrine (hormonal) system**.
The **neuron (nerve cell)** is the functional unit: **dendrites** receive, **cell body + axon** transmit, and a **synapse** passes the signal (chemical) to the next neuron/muscle.
**Receptors** detect stimuli (gustatory = taste, olfactory = smell, photoreceptors = light, etc.).

sections.heading: 2. Reflex Action and Nervous Organisation
points: **Reflex action** — a quick, automatic response to a stimulus (e.g. touching a hot object); the **reflex arc** passes through the **spinal cord** (not the brain) for speed.
**Central Nervous System (CNS)** = brain + spinal cord; **Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)** = nerves.

sub: **Mid-brain and hind-brain** — **cerebellum** (posture/balance/precision), **medulla** (involuntary: heartbeat, breathing, blood pressure), **pons**.

points: The brain and spinal cord are protected by bone (skull, vertebral column) and fluid.

sections.heading: 3. Coordination in Plants
points: Plants lack a nervous system; they respond via **chemical (hormonal)** coordination and movements.

sub: **Nastic (non-directional)** — e.g. **touch-me-not (Mimosa)** leaves fold on touch (not growth-related).
**Tropic (directional, growth)** — **phototropism** (towards light), **geotropism** (roots down, shoots up), **hydrotropism** (towards water), **chemotropism** (e.g. pollen tube).

sections.heading: 4. Plant and Animal Hormones

sub: **Gibberellin** — stem growth; **Cytokinin** — cell division (promotes growth); **Abscisic acid (ABA)** — inhibits growth, closes stomata, causes wilting/dormancy.

**Thyroid** (thyroxine — needs **iodine**; deficiency = goitre); **Pituitary** (growth hormone — deficiency dwarfism, excess gigantism); **Pancreas** (**insulin** — controls blood sugar; deficiency = diabetes); **Adrenal** (**adrenaline** — fight-or-flight); **Testes/ovary** (testosterone/oestrogen).

points: **Feedback mechanism** regulates hormone secretion (e.g. blood sugar controls insulin).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Neuron = functional unit; synapse passes signal; reflex arc via spinal cord.
Auxin = phototropism/elongation; abscisic acid = closes stomata, wilting.
Thyroxine needs iodine (deficiency = goitre); insulin controls blood sugar (diabetes).
Adrenaline = fight-or-flight; growth hormone from pituitary.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Reflex actions** are processed by the **spinal cord** (for speed), not the brain.
**Insulin** (from pancreas) regulates blood sugar; deficiency causes **diabetes**.
